answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit/accept-a-payment identifies SEPA Direct Debit acceptance and links Checkout, Elements and React Native only (new raw lines 5-16). Preconditions, parties and payment states come from the expanded 2026-05-03 capture. Checkout line items use EUR with dynamic or manual method selection and payment, setup and subscription support (old raw lines 12-49). The May Elements guide recommends Stripe's prebuilt Checkout page for mandate collection when using the Stripe Creditor ID (old raw lines 950-958). For Elements and React Native the merchant server creates an EUR PaymentIntent. The buyer provides IBAN and acknowledges the mandate. The Payment Element collects bank details and presents mandate text, while Stripe.js confirmPayment submits the existing intent. React Native has its own confirmPayment call (old raw lines 754-813, 1090-1110 and 1172-1181). Stripe moves a successfully submitted intent from requires_confirmation to processing, then to succeeded on success, with payment_intent.payment_failed on decline (old raw lines 1267-1279). When configured for reuse, Elements attaches the PaymentMethod on processing to the account or customer appropriate to Accounts v2 or Customers v1, even if payment later fails (old raw lines 1281-1287). source-stripe-sepa-accept-payment.md retains checkout and webhook details but mislabels standalone mobile variants and gives conflicting test-table counts.
answers.Q2: The November change at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit/accept-a-payment is presentational and navigational: it links the same three variant families without the May bodies (new raw lines 9-16). No substantive behavior change is established. Preserve the May capture and correct source-stripe-sepa-accept-payment.md to describe Checkout, React Native and Elements (old raw lines 500-509 and 950-958), and 19 test country headings with eight scenarios per table. Preserve the May three-to-fifteen-day best-effort debit date and business-day deferral conditions (old raw lines 487-498 and 1546-1557). Keep the Checkout introduction’s typical five-business-day funds arrival (old raw lines 18-20), the Elements webhook outcome boundary (old raw lines 1267-1287), and the separately sourced May product-reference T+6 standard settlement and six-business-day guidance in their own contexts. Retain the reciprocal SEPA concept route, separate setup and subscription documentation, and May raw alongside November navigation.
